reasoning_traces.think: Chapter 4 introduces the application of sensitivity analysis from Theorem 3.3 to mean field games (MFGs), focusing on verifying feedback regularity conditions essential for solving the associated coupled backward-forward systems. The framework considers a continuum of players governed by a common stochastic differential equation with state-dependent drift and diffusion coefficients. Each player observes their own state and the empirical distribution of all players, leading to a decentralized decision-making environment. The core innovation lies in deriving sufficient conditions under which the optimal control strategy depends continuously on the empirical distribution, ensuring well-posedness of the MFG system. This is formalized through the feedback regularity condition, which bounds the difference in optimal controls by the distance between empirical distributions in the dual norm of \(C^2\). The derivation hinges on the structure of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation and the generator \(L[t, \mu]\), which encapsulates the infinitesimal dynamics of the measure flow. Examples illustrate how specific structures—such as quadratic costs and linear drift—yield tractable forms of the HJB equation, including generalized backward Burgers' equations. These insights enable rigorous treatment of large-population strategic interactions in continuous time.
